title: Digital Pakistan Policy
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A national policy for expanding Pakistan's digital economy and public-service digitisation through infrastructure, skills, e-government, sectoral applications, technology adoption, and support for the IT industry.
key_provisions: Sets a whole-of-government direction for digital infrastructure, human-resource development, software exports, e-government, and digitisation of major socioeconomic sectors.
Calls for adoption and domestic capacity building in artificial intelligence, robotics, the Internet of Things, cloud computing, and big-data technologies.
Promotes integration of government databases, cloud-based citizen services, and common infrastructure for public- and private-sector applications.

title: Digital Nation Pakistan Act, 2025
summary: An Act establishing national institutions and planning mechanisms for Pakistan's digital transformation, including digital public infrastructure, data exchange, and coordinated digital governance.
key_provisions: Establishes the National Digital Commission to provide strategic direction for national digital transformation.
Establishes the Pakistan Digital Authority to formulate, coordinate, and monitor the National Digital Masterplan and sectoral plans.
Provides for digital public infrastructure, digital citizen journeys, and a secure and interoperable data exchange layer.
affects: Private enterprises accessing public digital services

title: Data Governance Policy 2026
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A draft national policy for governing federal public-sector data across its lifecycle, including sovereignty, residency, openness, sharing, privacy, cross-border transfers, emerging technologies, and institutional implementation.
key_provisions: Proposes sovereignty by default, federated data custody, authoritative-source discipline, minimum disclosure, interoperability, and privacy-by-design as national principles.
Would apply to federal public bodies and organisations processing government data on their behalf, while promoting coordination with provincial governments.
Proposes governance requirements for data residency, cross-border transfer, artificial intelligence, open data, and data sharing.

title: WASL — Pakistan National Data Exchange Layer: Reference Architecture
summary: The published pilot-maturity reference architecture for Pakistan's national data exchange layer, defining a centrally routed but data-blind platform with federated data custody and consent-governed exchange.
key_provisions: Defines central control and routing components while keeping operational data custody and cryptographic key control with participating entities.
Requires end-to-end encrypted exchange, citizen consent controls, transaction proofs, standardised schemas, and interoperable client nodes.
Defines integration surfaces for authorised AI consumers and a roadmap for post-quantum cryptographic agility.

title: Pakistan Cloud First Policy
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A federal policy directing public-sector entities toward cloud-based ICT investment, with governance arrangements for service-provider accreditation, data classification, procurement, security, and cloud adoption.
key_provisions: Applies to federal public-sector entities making new ICT investments and provides guidance for regulated and private-sector organisations.
Establishes a Cloud Office to oversee cloud adoption, accreditation, compliance, exemptions, and coordination with provinces.
Requires public-sector entities to procure from accredited cloud service providers and links cloud selection to government-data classification.
Allows consultation with the Cloud Office for legitimate cross-border data-flow use cases and associated security controls.

title: Accreditation Criteria for Cloud Service Providers
issuing_body: Interim Cloud Office, Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: Criteria and procedures for accrediting cloud service providers that seek to supply cloud services to Pakistan's public-sector entities.
key_provisions: Sets general, security, privacy, service-management, quality-management, and data-centre requirements for applicant cloud providers.
Requires documentation supporting certifications, service commitments, technical capacity, and compliance with the Pakistan Cloud First Policy.
Provides for accreditation, audits, suspension, and termination, with the Cloud Office maintaining the accredited-provider list.

title: Standard Bidding Document/Procurement Framework for Cloud Services
issuing_body: Public Procurement Regulatory Authority and Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A national standard procurement document for federal public bodies acquiring cloud services, designed to align tendering and contract practices with public-procurement rules and the Pakistan Cloud First Policy.
key_provisions: Standardises proposal instructions, evaluation procedures, technical requirements, and contract conditions for cloud-service procurement.
Provides cloud-specific proposal data and service requirements that procuring agencies can complete for individual acquisitions.
Links federal cloud procurement to the Public Procurement Rules and the Pakistan Cloud First Policy.

title: Framework on Outsourcing to Cloud Service Providers
summary: A regulatory framework setting minimum risk-management requirements for cloud outsourcing by banks, digital banks, microfinance banks, development finance institutions, electronic money institutions, and payment-system operators and providers.
key_provisions: Applies a risk-based framework to outsourcing material and non-material workloads to domestic or offshore cloud service providers.
Requires governance, risk assessment, due diligence, contractual protections, information security, audit access, business continuity, and exit planning.
Required regulated entities to align existing cloud-outsourcing arrangements with the framework by 31 December 2023.

title: Draft Cloud Adoption Guidelines for Incorporated Companies
issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
summary: Draft guidance for companies and other business entities incorporated with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan when assessing, adopting, migrating to, and managing cloud services.
key_provisions: Describes analysis, planning, adoption, migration, and ongoing management phases for cloud transitions.
Recommends board-level cloud governance, data classification, data portability, service-level agreements, and compliance checks.
Directs entities subject to sector-specific regulators to follow those regulators' cloud requirements.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: Pakistan's approved national policy for developing and adopting artificial intelligence through innovation, skills, responsible-use safeguards, sectoral transformation, compute and data infrastructure, and international cooperation.
key_provisions: Organises implementation around six pillars: innovation, awareness and readiness, secure AI, transformation, infrastructure, and international partnerships.
Calls for a National AI Fund, centres of excellence, research and commercialisation support, workforce training, scholarships, and internships.
Proposes transparency, human oversight, data protection, open-source governance, and regulatory sandboxes for AI systems.
Provides for national AI compute capacity, datasets, hubs, and an implementation mechanism led through the Ministry.

title: Draft Semiconductor Policy and Action Plan
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A draft policy and action plan for developing Pakistan's semiconductor workforce, design and packaging capabilities, research base, domestic industry, and participation in global supply chains.
key_provisions: Proposes incentives, a single-window interface, intellectual-property support, tax measures, and a national semiconductor fund.
Calls for shared electronic-design-automation infrastructure, semiconductor parks, and integration with special economic zones.
Proposes education and research clusters, workforce training, startup support, public-private partnerships, and international collaboration.
Sets a long-term objective of indigenous design, testing, packaging, and fabrication capability for critical integrated circuits by 2047.

title: National Broadband Policy 2021 — Consultation Draft v3.0
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A consultation draft proposing national broadband targets and policy measures for digital inclusion, market development, trust, infrastructure, and adoption of future network technologies.
key_provisions: Organises proposed measures under inclusivity and accessibility, usability and market enablement, digital trust, and transformation and evolution.
Proposes phased broadband, device-adoption, speed, affordability, skills, and connectivity targets through 2025 and 2030.
Addresses spectrum, fibre, data centres, internet exchanges, satellite connectivity, competition, quality of service, and emerging technologies.

title: 5G Readiness Plan for Pakistan
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: A World Bank-supported final draft assessing Pakistan's readiness for 5G and presenting recommendations on spectrum, investment, infrastructure, regulation, and use cases; the document states that its recommendations do not necessarily represent the government's position.
key_provisions: Assesses market readiness, spectrum availability and pricing, device affordability, fibre backhaul, and infrastructure conditions.
Reviews regulatory measures involving rights of way, infrastructure sharing, competition, cloud infrastructure, and access to towers and fibre.
Presents recommendations for sequencing spectrum release and supporting 5G applications and use cases.

title: 5G Strategic Plan and Policy Guidelines — Consultation Draft
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
summary: Draft policy guidelines proposing a coordinated path toward 5G deployment through spectrum planning, regulatory preparation, infrastructure facilitation, investment incentives, trials, skills, and public awareness.
key_provisions: Proposes spectrum-band preparation, consultant-led auction design, licensing recommendations, and a spectrum-refarming framework.
Calls for review of rights-of-way rules and possible fiscal incentives for 5G equipment, devices, and local manufacturing.
Proposes innovation and test centres, non-commercial trials, 5G skills programmes, and public-awareness activity.
The document's original milestones targeted preparatory actions in 2022 and a commercial launch in early 2023.
